Edward Mena is a Venezuelan singer and activist known for his performances in Latin music and American classics. He gained international attention as the first Venezuelan-American artist to perform the U.S. national anthem at a presidential event invited by The White House.
Career
In 2019, Mena made history by performing The Star-Spangled Banner at a presidential event, becoming the first Venezuelan-American artist to do so. This performance garnered international attention and marked a significant milestone in his career.
Beyond his musical endeavors, Mena serves as Vice President of the ARTS Autism Foundation, demonstrating his commitment to community engagement and support for individuals with autism.
